english.title: Use a motor vehicle on a road / public place without third party insurance
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a road, or other public place, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ROAD OR PUBLIC PLACE AND LOCATION..), when there was not in force in relation to that use such a policy of insurance as complied with the requirements of Part VI of the Road Traffic Act 1988
english.legislation: Contrary to section 143 of, the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to, the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) See also offence wordings: H100081 and H100082.
(ii) There is a common term in insurance policies that usually states something along the lines that the driver is covered if s/he holds or has held a driving licence to drive the vehicle (i.e. that class of vehicle) and is not disqualified. We are assuming everything else in the certificate is in order. If this term is in the certificate of insurance (and the driver is not disqualified by a court), s/he is covered by the insurance whether or not s/he does or does not hold a current UK/foreign/provisional licence for that class of vehicle, as long as s/he held one in the past - (see Edwards v Griffiths 1953). However, the term can vary on occasion, so it is worth reading the certificate carefully.
(iv) Until 1st November 2021, securities or deposits could be used as an alternative to conventional motor insurance. For offences before that date see H33.
